text: About once a year, the New Moon falls in your first house, the part of the chart that stands for you: your body, your face, your name, the way you walk into a room. A New Moon is the start of the lunar month, the few days when the Moon slips between Earth and Sun and goes dark before a new crescent forms. When that dark start happens here, the month that follows takes you as its subject. You may notice the shift as a change in appetite for your own life. Projects that belong to other people feel less urgent, and questions about what you want, how you present yourself, and what you would begin if it were entirely up to you feel more so. Some years it shows up physically: a wish to cut your hair, change how you dress, or start moving your body differently. Other years it is quieter, a private sense that one version of you is finished and another is forming. Because the light is low at a New Moon, the beginning rarely announces itself. Whatever starts now tends to start small, on instinct, without an audience, and grows over the following weeks as the Moon does. That makes these few days better for planting than for proving. Naming one thing you want for yourself, in plain words, does more good now than pushing for visible results. Energy can dip right at the start, and that is normal; seeds do their first work underground. As the month goes on, matters of self and direction keep coming back around in different costumes, developing what the dark days seeded. Since this visitation returns about yearly, it works like an annual restart of the personal thread of your life, separate from your birthday but similar in spirit. Over time you learn its rhythm: the years you used the quiet start to point yourself somewhere deliberate tend to read differently, later, than the years the month simply happened to you.

Each New Moon opens a month somewhere in your chart, and roughly once a year it opens one in your second house, the house of money, possessions, and what you consider yours. The days around it are the dark of the Moon, when one lunar cycle has ended and the next has not yet shown light, and here that reset lands on material life. The month ahead tends to keep returning to questions of earning, spending, owning, and worth. A beginning in this territory is usually undramatic. It looks like starting a fresh ledger, asking for the first time what a skill of yours might be worth, noticing which of your things you actually use, or feeling the first pull toward building a cushion. The New Moon does not deliver money; it renews your relationship with it. Intentions set now do best when they are concrete and small enough to act on within the month: one account looked at honestly, one recurring cost questioned, one talent taken more seriously. The second house is also about worth in the wider sense, the value you assign yourself when no one is bidding. In the low light of these few days, that question can surface quietly: what you tolerate, what you charge, what you think you deserve to keep. Feelings about security run close to the surface, and if money is tight the dark of the Moon can make the worry louder for a day or two. The worry is information, not a forecast. What steadies it is the same thing the moment is for: choosing one modest starting point and letting the month build on it. Because this New Moon returns about yearly, you get a regular chance to begin again with the material side of life rather than only continuing it. Year over year, those small annual beginnings compound the way material things do, slowly and by accumulation, and you grow a steadier hand with what you have.

Words, errands, neighbors, siblings, the near world you move through daily: that is the third house, and the New Moon begins its month there about once a year. New Moons are the dark seam between one lunar cycle and the next, a few days when beginnings form out of sight, and when that seam falls here the weeks that follow turn talkative, mobile, and curious. Starts in this house look like first conversations: the message that opens a correspondence, the question that starts a course of study, the first page of something you have been meaning to write, the knock on a neighbor's door. None of it is grand, and it is not supposed to be. The third house works in short trips and small exchanges, and its beginnings are sized to match. If there is a sibling or a person from your everyday circle you have drifted from, the impulse to reopen contact often stirs around now. Curiosity is the natural mood. You may find yourself wanting new input, a book, a class, a different route through familiar streets, and following that want is exactly how this cycle gets used. Setting an intention here works best as a question: what do you want to understand by the time the month is out, and who do you want to be in better conversation with. The low light of a New Moon asks for a little patience with speech itself. Things said in the dark days can be half-formed, so first drafts belong in drawers for a beat before they travel. Over the following weeks, the ideas seeded now gather words and audiences of their own. And because it comes back about yearly, it reopens the channels on a schedule: a fresh start for your mail, your reading, your local ties, and the ongoing project of saying what you mean.

There is a point at the bottom of your chart where the fourth house sits: home, family, roots, the private life underneath the public one. About once a year the New Moon lands there and opens its monthly cycle in that quiet ground. A New Moon is a beginning made in the dark, the days when the old lunar month has ended and the new one has not yet become visible, and a beginning in the fourth house suits that darkness. It happens indoors, offstage, in rooms rather than in view. The month that follows tends to pull your attention homeward. Practical versions are easy to spot: moving, rearranging, repairing, starting a search for a different place, beginning a household differently after someone arrives or leaves. Emotional versions are subtler. A new understanding with a parent or relative can begin now, or a decision about what family means to you, or simply a renewed wish to make wherever you live feel more like yours. Old material sometimes surfaces around this lunation, memories and family patterns showing up and asking to be handled a new way, which is less an intrusion than the point: foundations get rebuilt from the bottom. Whatever you begin, keep the scale honest. One room made livable, one conversation started gently, one habit of homecoming: these are fourth house seeds, and they grow through the month the way the Moon does, from nothing visible toward fullness. It is also fine if the beginning is only rest. This house holds the part of you that needs somewhere to land, and some years the truest intention available is to tend that need on purpose. Because the visit repeats about yearly, it makes a kind of annual housewarming for your inner life. The years accumulate, and you slowly learn what home actually requires for you, as distinct from what you inherited, which is one of the longer and more useful projects a person gets.

The fifth house holds what you do for the joy of it: creative work, romance, play, children, and every risk taken just to feel alive. When the New Moon arrives there, about once a year, the month opens with an invitation from that territory. A New Moon is the dark beginning of the lunar cycle, a seed moment rather than a harvest, so what stirs now tends to be a first flicker: an idea for something you would make, a pull toward someone new, an urge to book the fun you keep postponing. The impulse can feel slight, and the low light means it arrives without proof that it will amount to anything. It does not need proof yet. Fifth house beginnings ask only that you take your own delight seriously enough to give it a start. In the weeks that follow, the sketch can become a draft, the flirtation a plan, the vague wish for play an actual afternoon of it. If children are part of your life, a fresh chapter with them often opens around this lunation, sometimes through nothing more than a change in how you play together. The house also covers the gamble of being seen, since making something and courting someone both risk rejection, and the quiet start of a New Moon is a kind opening for that risk: you can begin privately, before any audience gathers. What tends to block this house is the belief that pleasure must be earned first. The annual return of this New Moon is a standing argument against that, a once-a-year reminder that enjoyment is not the leftovers of a life but one of its load-bearing parts. Used year after year, the cycle builds a body of things you made and moments you were glad to be there for, which is its own answer to the question of what the time was for.

Some months begin loudly. The month that starts with a New Moon in your sixth house begins with a list. This is the house of work in its daily sense: routines, duties, health habits, the maintenance of your life and of the body that carries it. About once a year the lunar cycle opens here and asks how the machinery is running. The light is low at the start of a lunar month, so the change this moment favors is small and structural rather than sweeping. A new morning order. A different lunch. The appointment finally scheduled, the desk cleared, the walk added back in. In the sixth house, modesty is not a limitation; it is the method. A routine altered by one degree and held for the month while the Moon waxes does more than a grand overhaul abandoned by the following week. Your body often speaks up around this lunation, not necessarily with trouble, more with a report: tiredness that says the schedule is wrong, tension that maps to one task, appetite asking for different fuel. Listening counts as work here. So does the job itself, since this house covers your labor and its conditions. A new project, a new colleague, a new arrangement of your hours can all begin under this Moon, and the quiet start suits them. Service belongs here too, the unglamorous help you give and receive, and some years the month's real beginning is deciding whose load you will help carry, or admitting where you need help with yours. It comes once a year, a service interval for your ordinary life. Nothing about it is dramatic, which is exactly its value; the dramatic houses depend on this one. A year in which the routines got one notch saner and the body one notch better tended is a year in which everything else had something to stand on, and this small dark Moon is where that year begins.

When the New Moon falls in your seventh house, the month begins across the table from you. This is the house of the other person: partner, spouse, close collaborator, the trusted opposite number, and also the open rival, anyone you meet one to one as an equal. A New Moon opens a monthly cycle in whatever house it touches, and it reaches this one about once a year, so roughly annually your relationships get a dark, quiet starting line of their own. Beginnings here take many shapes. A meeting that later turns out to have mattered. A first date, a proposal of any kind, an agreement, a handshake that starts a working partnership. Inside an established bond, the beginning is often a renegotiation: a conversation that resets terms, a decision to try again differently, a season of the relationship opening while another closes. Even conflict can be a seventh house start, since naming a dispute honestly is the first act of resolving it. The low light of the New Moon shapes how these starts feel. They are seldom certain at the time. You commit a little before you can see much, which is what all partnership asks sooner or later, and the weeks that follow let the thing become visible by degrees. Intentions set now do best when they concern your half of the table: how you want to show up, what you are ready to offer, what you will no longer carry alone. The house also has a mirroring habit. People you meet or clash with around this lunation tend to show you something of yourself, especially the parts you prefer to see in others rather than own. Taken yearly, these small beginnings add up to an education in partnership. You learn what you actually need from an equal, what you reliably give, and how to start things with another person in good faith, which no one learns alone.

The eighth house is the deep end of the chart: money and lives entangled with other people's, what is owed and what is left behind, real intimacy, and the endings that make renewals possible. About once a year the New Moon opens its month down there. A beginning that happens in the dark suits no house better than this one, where the important events are rarely visible from the street. The month that follows tends to concern what is merged and what must be settled. On the practical side, that can mean the start of dealings with joint finances: a loan, a repayment plan, taxes, an inheritance matter, the money side of a partnership getting a fresh look. None of these are misfortunes. They are the ordinary machinery of lives tangled with other lives, and this cycle is when the machinery gets renewed attention. On the inner side, the eighth house is where trust is built or tested. A new depth of honesty with someone can begin now, the kind that trades performance for truth, and so can the slow work of loosening a grip: on a grievance, a fear, an old version of a bond that no longer fits. Beginnings here often wear the costume of endings. Something is released, and only afterward does it become clear that the release was the start. The low light of these few days can stir strong feeling, and privacy is the right container for it; this is a house that does its work better in a journal or a trusted conversation than in public. If you set an intention, let it be about what you are ready to put down as much as what you want to pick up. The yearly return of this Moon makes renewal a schedule rather than a crisis, and each pass you get a little better at the exchange this house teaches: letting go of what is finished so the living parts of your life get the room.

The ninth house is where your life gets bigger than its daily radius: long journeys, higher learning, publishing, law, philosophy, the beliefs you steer by. About once a year the New Moon arrives there and starts its monthly cycle on that wide ground. New Moons are seed days, the dark opening of the lunar month, so what begins now is usually a first step toward distance: a trip imagined and then priced, an application started, a course begun, a question about meaning finally asked out loud. For the next few weeks your attention keeps drifting toward the horizon. Restlessness is a common first symptom. The familiar can feel briefly too small, and the appetite for elsewhere, whether a place, a subject, or a way of thinking, comes back with its yearly strength. Following it does not require an airport. Ninth house travel includes the kind done through books, teachers, languages, and people whose lives run on different assumptions, and a beginning made at a desk counts fully. Belief is the quieter cargo of this house. Around this lunation you may notice a conviction that has expired, a view you have outgrown, or a growing one that wants room. The low light of the New Moon is a good hour for such revisions, since no one changes their mind gracefully in public. If something in you wants to teach, publish, or say what you have learned to a wider circle, the first outline belongs to these days; the audience belongs to later in the month. Keep the seed small and the direction honest, and let distance do its work over the weeks that follow. Because this visitation is annual, the far side of your life gets its yearly opening. Year by year, the trips taken, the subjects studied, and the beliefs revised knit into a view of the world you actually built, rather than one you happened to be issued.

At the top of your chart sits the tenth house: career, reputation, public standing, the work the world knows you by. Once a year, give or take, the New Moon opens its monthly cycle up there, and the month begins with your ambitions in the room. It is a strange pairing at first glance. New Moons are dark, private starting points, and the tenth house is the most visible ground you have. In practice the combination means the public thread of your life gets a quiet, offstage beginning: the application drafted before anyone knows you are looking, the pitch outlined, the conversation with yourself about what you want your work to amount to. What starts near this lunation tends to surface later, once the light has grown. Concrete versions are familiar: a new role, a new responsibility, a project with your name on it, the first move toward a different line of work. Subtler versions matter as much. A change in how you want to be seen professionally can begin now, or the slow admission that a goal you have been climbing toward belongs to someone else's definition of success. The tenth house also holds authority, yours and other people's. Dealings with bosses, institutions, or your own role as the responsible one often feature in this month, and beginnings there, a boundary set, a standard raised, count as career moves even when no title changes. An intention set in these low days does best when it names direction rather than outcome: the kind of work, the kind of reputation, the kind of usefulness you are aiming your effort at. The yearly rhythm is the real gift. Careers are long, and a once-a-year dark morning spent asking where the climb is pointed keeps the ladder against the right wall, which the daily climbing never checks on its own.

A New Moon in your eleventh house starts the month among other people. This is the house of friends, allies, groups, and the future you are hoping toward, and the lunar cycle opens here about once a year, giving your social life and your long hopes an annual starting line. New Moons favor beginnings made quietly, and eleventh house beginnings usually look social from the outside and personal from within: joining something, showing up somewhere new, writing to a friend you have missed, saying yes to the invitation you usually decline. A single introduction made near this lunation can turn out to carry the whole month, since this house works through networks, where one thread leads to many. Friendship itself often asks for renewal now. Some years that means widening the circle; other years it means tending the middle of it, beginning a more honest chapter with the few who matter, or noticing which ties run on habit alone. Both are valid seeds. The house's other cargo is the future: wishes, plans, the shape of the life you are working toward with others rather than alone. The old practice of naming wishes at a New Moon fits nowhere better than here. In the low light, before the month makes its demands, there is room to ask what you actually hope for, and who shares it, because eleventh house hopes are the collaborative kind, causes and projects and futures that need more hands than yours. An intention set now might be as small as one gathering attended or one plan spoken aloud to a friend, which makes it real in a way private resolutions are not. Since the visitation is yearly, the returns compound socially: circles built one introduction at a time, hopes revised one year at a time. Slowly you find yourself surrounded by people who point the same direction you do, and that changes what you can attempt.

Roughly once a year the New Moon falls in your twelfth house, the chart's most hidden room: solitude, rest, the unconscious, unfinished business, everything that happens offstage. The lunar month that begins here starts further out of sight than usual. A New Moon is already a dark beginning; in the twelfth it is a beginning you may not even notice at the time, and that is not a failure of attention but the nature of the ground. The month ahead tends to run on a lower frequency. Energy for public effort can thin, sleep and dreams get louder, and the wish to withdraw a little, from noise, from company, from the performance of being fine, comes back with its annual weight. The tradition reads this house as the place of endings that precede beginnings, and the month often behaves accordingly: something wraps up quietly, a burden you were carrying without naming it becomes visible, an old pattern surfaces on its way out. Letting the wrap-up happen is the work. Beginnings here are inward ones. A practice of meditation, prayer, therapy, or simple unscheduled quiet can start now and hold better than at most other times of year. So can quiet compassion, the unpublicized help this house has always covered, given or received without an audience. If you set an intention, set it gently and privately, and do not expect to watch it sprout. Twelfth house seeds germinate in the dark and tend to show their growth later, in other months, as changed feeling rather than visible events. There is nothing ominous in any of this. Rest is not an interruption of your life, and a yearly month tilted toward it is closer to a tide than a trial. Treat these weeks as the exhale of your year, and you generally arrive at the next stretch clearer, lighter, and better company to yourself, without being able to point to the moment it happened.
